definitions: To support something with actions or money, not just words.
To show that you believe in something by being willing to risk your own money or take action.
examples: If you really think it's a good investment, put your money where your mouth is and buy some shares.
He's always boasting about his business ideas, but he needs to put his money where his mouth is.
It's time for the government to put its money where its mouth is and fund the new hospital.
lemma: put your money where your mouth is
synonyms: back up your words with action
source: put your money where your mouth is
